source_blocks.html:
Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G
A
Some archaeological sites have always been easily observable—for example, the Parthenon in Athens, Greece; the pyramids of Giza in Egypt; and the megaliths of Stonehenge in southern England. But these sites are exceptions to the norm. Most archaeological sites have been located by means of careful searching, while many others have been discovered by accident. Olduvai Gorge, in Tanzania, was found by a butterfly hunter who literally fell into its deep valley in 1911. Thousands of Aztec artifacts came to light during the digging of the Mexico City subway in the 1970s.
有些考古遗址向来易于观察——例如希腊雅典的帕特农神庙、埃及的吉萨金字塔，以及英格兰南部的巨石阵。但这些遗址只是常态中的例外。多数考古遗址是通过仔细搜寻定位的，而许多其他遗址则是偶然发现的。坦桑尼亚的奥杜威峡谷，是一位蝴蝶猎人在1911年失足跌入其深谷时被发现的。数千件阿兹特克文物则是在1970年代修建墨西哥城地铁时被发掘出来的。
B
In another case, American archaeologists René million and George Cowgill spent years systematically mapping the entire city of Teotihuacan in the valley of Mexico near what is now Mexico City. At its peak around AD 600, this city was one of the largest human settlements in the world. The researchers mapped not only the city's vast and ornate ceremonial areas, but also hundreds of simpler apartment complexes where common people lived.
另有一例，美国考古学家勒内·米永和乔治·考吉尔耗时数年，系统测绘了如今墨西哥城附近墨西哥谷地中的特奥蒂瓦坎古城。公元600年前后鼎盛期，该城曾是世界上最大的人类聚居地之一。研究者不仅测绘了这座城市宏大而华丽的礼仪区，也测绘了数百座普通民众居住的相对简陋的公寓建筑群。
C
How do archaeologists know where to find what they are looking for when there is nothing visible on the surface of the ground? Typically, they survey and sample (make test excavations on) large areas of terrain to determine where excavation will yield useful information. Surveys and test samples have also become important for understanding the larger landscapes that contain archaeological sites.
当地表上看不到任何东西时，考古学家如何知道去哪里寻找目标？通常，他们会对大片区域进行勘测与取样（即进行试掘），以确定何处发掘能产出有用信息。勘测与试掘对于理解包含考古遗址的更广阔地貌也变得十分重要。
D
Surveys can cover a single large settlement or entire landscapes. In one case, many researchers working around the ancient Maya city of Copán, Honduras, have located hundreds of small rural village and individual dwellings by using aerial photographs and by making surveys on foot. The resulting settlement maps show how the distribution and density of the rural population around the city changed dramatically between AD500 and 850, when Copán collapsed.
勘测可以覆盖单个大型聚落，也可以覆盖整片地貌。有一例中，许多围绕洪都拉斯科潘玛雅古城工作的研究者，借助航拍照片和步行勘测，定位了数百个小型乡村聚落与独立居所。由此绘成的聚落地图显示，在科潘于公元500至850年间走向崩溃的过程中，城市周边农村人口的分布与密度发生了剧烈变化。
E
To find their sites, archaeologists today rely heavily on systematic survey methods and a variety of high-technology tools and techniques. Airborne technologies, such as different types of radar and photographic equipment carried by airplanes or spacecraft, allow archaeologists to learn about what lies beneath the ground without digging. Aerial surveys locate general areas of interest or larger buried features, such as ancient buildings or fields.
为找到遗址，今天的考古学家高度依赖系统的勘测方法和各种高技术工具与手段。机载技术——如飞机或航天器搭载的各类雷达与摄影设备——使考古学家无需挖掘便能了解地下埋藏。航空勘测可定位大致的感兴趣区域或更大的地下特征，如古代建筑或田地。
F
Most archaeological sites, however, are discovered by archaeologists who have set out to look for them. Such searches can take years. British archaeologist Howard Carter knew that the tomb of the Egyptian pharaoh Tutankhamun existed from information found in other sites. Carter sifted through rubble in the Valley of the Kings for seven years before he located the tomb in 1922. In the late 1800s British archaeologist Sir Arthur Evans combed antique dealers' stores in Athens, Greece. He was searching for engraved seals attributed to the ancient Mycenaean culture that dominated Greece from the 1400s to 1200s BC. Evans's interpretations of those engravings eventually led them to find the Minoan palace at Knossos on the island of Crete, in 1900.
然而，多数考古遗址是由特意前去寻找的考古学家发现的。这种搜寻可能历时数年。英国考古学家霍华德·卡特从其他遗址所获信息中得知埃及法老图坦卡蒙之墓存在。他在帝王谷的瓦砾中筛寻了七年，才于1922年定位该墓。19世纪末，英国考古学家阿瑟·埃文斯爵士在希腊雅典的古董商店铺中仔细搜寻，寻找据信属于公元前1400至1200年主导希腊的迈锡尼文明的刻印。埃文斯对这些刻印的解读，最终引导人们在1900年找到了克里特岛克诺索斯的米诺斯宫殿。
G
Ground surveys allow archaeologists to pinpoint the places where digs will be successful. Most ground surveys involve a lot of walking, looking for surface clues such as small fragments of pottery. They often include a certain amount of digging to test for buried materials at selected points across a landscape. Archaeologists also may locate buried remains by using such technologies as ground radar, magnetic-field recording, and metal detector. Archaeologists commonly use computers to map sites and the landscapes around sites. Two and three-dimensional maps are helpful tools in planning excavations, illustrating how sites look, and presenting the results of archaeological research.
地面勘测让考古学家能精准定位挖掘将有所收获的地点。多数地面勘测需要大量步行，寻找陶片之类的地表线索。它们通常还包括一定量的挖掘，以测试地貌上若干选点的地下埋藏。考古学家也可借助地面雷达、磁场记录与金属探测器等技术定位地下遗存。考古学家通常还用计算机为遗址及其周边地貌绘制地图。二维与三维地图是规划发掘、展示遗址样貌以及呈现考古研究成果的有用工具。

A
Some archaeological sites have always been easily observable—for example, the Parthenon in Athens, Greece; the pyramids of Giza in Egypt; and the megaliths of Stonehenge in southern England. But these sites are exceptions to the norm. Most archaeological sites have been located by means of careful searching, while many others have been discovered by accident. Olduvai Gorge, in Tanzania, was found by a butterfly hunter who literally fell into its deep valley in 1911. Thousands of Aztec artifacts came to light during the digging of the Mexico City subway in the 1970s.
有些考古遗址向来易于观察——例如希腊雅典的帕特农神庙、埃及的吉萨金字塔，以及英格兰南部的巨石阵。但这些遗址只是常态中的例外。多数考古遗址是通过仔细搜寻定位的，而许多其他遗址则是偶然发现的。坦桑尼亚的奥杜威峡谷，是一位蝴蝶猎人在1911年失足跌入其深谷时被发现的。数千件阿兹特克文物则是在1970年代修建墨西哥城地铁时被发掘出来的。
B
In another case, American archaeologists René million and George Cowgill spent years systematically mapping the entire city of Teotihuacan in the valley of Mexico near what is now Mexico City. At its peak around AD 600, this city was one of the largest human settlements in the world. The researchers mapped not only the city's vast and ornate ceremonial areas, but also hundreds of simpler apartment complexes where common people lived.
另有一例，美国考古学家勒内·米永和乔治·考吉尔耗时数年，系统测绘了如今墨西哥城附近墨西哥谷地中的特奥蒂瓦坎古城。公元600年前后鼎盛期，该城曾是世界上最大的人类聚居地之一。研究者不仅测绘了这座城市宏大而华丽的礼仪区，也测绘了数百座普通民众居住的相对简陋的公寓建筑群。
C
How do archaeologists know where to find what they are looking for when there is nothing visible on the surface of the ground? Typically, they survey and sample (make test excavations on) large areas of terrain to determine where excavation will yield useful information. Surveys and test samples have also become important for understanding the larger landscapes that contain archaeological sites.
当地表上看不到任何东西时，考古学家如何知道去哪里寻找目标？通常，他们会对大片区域进行勘测与取样（即进行试掘），以确定何处发掘能产出有用信息。勘测与试掘对于理解包含考古遗址的更广阔地貌也变得十分重要。
D
Surveys can cover a single large settlement or entire landscapes. In one case, many researchers working around the ancient Maya city of Copán, Honduras, have located hundreds of small rural village and individual dwellings by using aerial photographs and by making surveys on foot. The resulting settlement maps show how the distribution and density of the rural population around the city changed dramatically between AD500 and 850, when Copán collapsed.

Airborne technologies, such as different types of radar and photographic equipment carried by airplanes or spacecraft, allow archaeologists to learn about what lies beneath the ground without digging. Aerial surveys locate general areas of interest or larger buried features, such as ancient buildings or fields.

They often include a certain amount of digging to test for buried materials at selected points across a landscape. Archaeologists also may locate buried remains by using such technologies as ground radar, magnetic-field recording, and metal detector. Archaeologists commonly use computers to map sites and the landscapes around sites. Two and three-dimensional maps are helpful tools in planning excavations, illustrating how sites look, and presenting the results of archaeological research.

Dear Mr. President,

Finally, holding regular sports meets and fun competitions, such as rope-skipping contests, could spark students' enthusiasm for exercise.

source_blocks.html:
参考范文

The drawing vividly depicts a touching scene of "mutual support." Thirty years ago, a young mother held her little daughter's hand; today, the grown-up daughter supports her aged mother. Together the two pictures convey a timeless virtue of Chinese families—filial piety and the passing of love between generations.

The implied meaning is thought-provoking. On the one hand, parents sacrifice their youth to nurture their children; on the other, when parents grow old, children have a duty to repay that devotion. This mutual care is the very foundation of a harmonious family. Regrettably, in modern society some young people take their parents' love for granted and even shift the burden of elder care onto society.

From my perspective, we should carry forward the tradition of filial piety. Parents should set an example by respecting their own elders, while society as a whole should encourage the young to care for the old. Only in this way can we build a warm and loving community.

【译文】

图画生动地描绘了一个"相携"的感人场景。三十年前，年轻的母亲牵着小女儿的手；如今，长大成人的女儿搀扶着年迈的母亲。两幅图共同传递着中国家庭永恒的美德——孝道与爱的代际传承。

其寓意发人深省。一方面，父母牺牲青春养育子女；另一方面，当父母年老，子女也有责任回报这份付出。这种相互关怀正是和谐家庭的基石。遗憾的是，现代社会中有些年轻人把父母的爱视为理所当然，甚至把养老的负担推给社会。

在我看来，我们应传承孝亲传统。父母应以身作则、敬重自己的长辈，社会也应整体倡导青年敬老爱老。唯其如此，我们才能建成一个温暖而有爱的大家庭。

paragraphs.html: The US $3-million Fundamental Physics Prize is indeed an interesting experiment, as Alexander Polyakov said when he accepted this year's award in March. And it is far from the only one of its type. As a News Feature article in Nature discusses, a string of lucrative awards for researchers have joined the Nobel Prizes in recent years. Many, like the Fundamental Physics Prize, are funded from the telephone-number-sized bank accounts of Internet entrepreneurs. These benefactors have succeeded in their chosen fields, they say, and they want to use their wealth to draw attention to those who have succeeded in science.

The US $3-million Fundamental Physics Prize is indeed an interesting experiment, as Alexander Polyakov said when he accepted this year's award in March. And it is far from the only one of its type. As a News Feature article in Nature discusses, a string of lucrative awards for researchers have joined the Nobel Prizes in recent years. Many, like the Fundamental Physics Prize, are funded from the telephone-number-sized bank accounts of Internet entrepreneurs. These benefactors have succeeded in their chosen fields, they say, and they want to use their wealth to draw attention to those who have succeeded in science.

正如亚历山大·波利亚科夫在今年3月领奖时所说，300万美元的"基础物理学奖"确实是一个有趣的尝试。但它远非同类奖项中的唯一一个。正如《自然》杂志一篇新闻特写所讨论的，近年来一系列为研究者设立的丰厚奖项已经加入了诺贝尔奖的行列。其中许多奖项，如基础物理学奖，资金都来自互联网企业家那些电话号码般长的银行账户。这些捐助者在自己的领域获得了成功，他们想用自己的财富让人们关注那些在科学上取得成功的人。

What's not to like? Quite a lot, according to a handful of scientists quoted in the News Feature. You cannot buy class, as the old saying goes, and these upstart entrepreneurs cannot buy their prizes the prestige of the Nobels. The new awards are an exercise in self-promotion for those behind them, say scientists. They could distort the achievement-based system of peer-review-led research. They could cement the status quo of peer-reviewed research. They do not fund peer-reviewed research. They perpetuate the myth of the lone genius.

有什么不讨人喜欢的呢？据这篇特写引用的少数科学家说，不讨人喜欢的地方还真不少。正如老话说的，你买不来阶层，这些暴发户企业家也买不来他们奖项身上诺贝尔奖那样的声望。科学家们说，这些新奖项是其幕后推手的自我炒作。它们可能扭曲以成就为基础、由同行评审主导的研究体系。它们可能巩固同行评审研究的现状。它们并不资助同行评审研究。它们还延续了"孤胆天才"的神话。

The goals of the prize-givers seem as scattered as the criticism. Some want to shock, others to draw people into science, or to better reward those who have made their careers in research.

颁奖者的目标似乎和批评意见一样五花八门。有人想制造轰动，有人想吸引人们投身科学，还有人想更好地回报那些以研究为事业的人。

As Nature has pointed out before, there are some legitimate concerns about how science prizes—both new and old—are distributed. The Breakthrough Prize in Life Sciences, launched this year, takes an unrepresentative view of what the life sciences include. But the Nobel Foundation's limit of three recipients per prize, each of whom must still be living, has long been outgrown by the collaborative nature of modern research—as will be demonstrated by the inevitable row over who is ignored when it comes to acknowledging the discovery of the Higgs boson. The Nobels were, of course, themselves set up by a very rich individual who had decided what he wanted to do with his own money. Time, rather than intention, has given them legitimacy.

正如《自然》杂志此前指出的，人们对科学奖项——无论新旧——如何分配存在一些合理担忧。今年设立的"生命科学突破奖"对生命科学包含的范围持一种不具代表性的看法。但诺贝尔基金会对每项奖最多三名获奖者、且每位必须在世的限制，早已被现代研究的协作性质所超越——在表彰希格斯玻色子的发现时，谁被忽略了所引发的不可避免的争执将证明这一点。当然，诺贝尔奖本身也是由一位非常富有的人设立的，他决定用自己的钱做什么。赋予诺贝尔奖合法性的，是时间而非初衷。

As much as some scientists may complain about the new awards, two things seem clear. First, most researchers would accept such a prize if they were offered one. Second, it is surely a good thing that the money and attention come to science rather than go elsewhere. It is fair to criticize and question the mechanism—that is the culture of research, after all—but it is the prize-givers' money to do with as they please. It is wise to take such gifts with gratitude and grace.

尽管一些科学家可能会抱怨这些新奖项，但有两点似乎很清楚。第一，如果真有这样的奖，大多数研究者都会接受。第二，金钱和关注流向科学而不是别处，这肯定是件好事。批评和质疑这种机制是公平的——毕竟这就是研究文化——但这是颁奖者自己的钱，他们想怎么用就怎么用。怀着感激和优雅接受这样的馈赠才是明智之举。

paragraphs.html: In 2010, leading congressional Democrats and Republicans sent letters to the AAAS asking that it identify actions that could be taken by "federal, state and local governments, universities, foundations, educators, individual benefactors and others" to "maintain national excellence in humanities and social scientific scholarship and education." Among the commission's 51 members are top-tier-university presidents, scholars, lawyers, judges, and business executives, as well as prominent figures from diplomacy, filmmaking, music and journalism.

Regrettably, however, the report's failure to address the true nature of the crisis facing liberal education may cause more harm than good.

美国文理研究院（AAAS）刚刚发布的报告《问题的核心》值得称赞，因为它肯定了人文社会科学对美国自由民主的繁荣与安全的重要性。然而令人遗憾的是，该报告未能触及自由教育所面临危机的真正本质，可能弊大于利。

In 2010, leading congressional Democrats and Republicans sent letters to the AAAS asking that it identify actions that could be taken by "federal, state and local governments, universities, foundations, educators, individual benefactors and others" to "maintain national excellence in humanities and social scientific scholarship and education." In response, the American Academy formed the Commission on the Humanities and Social Sciences. Among the commission's 51 members are top-tier-university presidents, scholars, lawyers, judges, and business executives, as well as prominent figures from diplomacy, filmmaking, music and journalism.

2010年，国会民主党和共和党领袖致信AAAS，要求其明确"联邦、州和地方政府、大学、基金会、教育工作者、个人捐助者及其他各方"可采取哪些行动，以"保持国家在人文和社会科学学术与教育领域的卓越地位"。作为回应，美国文理研究院成立了人文与社会科学委员会。委员会的51名成员包括顶尖大学校长、学者、律师、法官、企业高管，以及来自外交、电影、音乐和新闻界的杰出人物。

The goals identified in the report are generally admirable. Because representative government presupposes an informed citizenry, the report supports full literacy; stresses the study of history and government, particularly American history and American government; and encourages the use of new digital technologies. To encourage innovation and competition, the report calls for increased investment in research, the crafting of coherent curricula that improve students' ability to solve problems and communicate effectively in the 21st century, increased funding for teachers and the encouragement of scholars to bring their learning to bear on the great challenges of the day. The report also advocates greater study of foreign languages, international affairs and the expansion of study abroad programs.

报告中确定的目标总体上令人钦佩。因为代议制政府的前提是知情的公民群体，报告支持全民读写能力；强调历史与政府研究，尤其是美国历史和美国政府；并鼓励使用新数字技术。为鼓励创新和竞争，报告呼吁增加研究投资、精心设计连贯课程以提升21世纪学生解决问题和有效沟通的能力、增加教师经费、鼓励学者用所学应对当今重大挑战。报告还提倡加强外语、国际事务学习并扩大留学项目。

Unfortunately, despite 2½ years in the making, "The Heart of the Matter" never gets to the heart of the matter: the illiberal nature of liberal education at our leading colleges and universities. The commission ignores that for several decades America's colleges and universities have produced graduates who don't know the content and character of liberal education and are thus deprived of its benefits. Sadly, the spirit of inquiry once at home on campus has been replaced by the use of the humanities and social sciences as vehicles for publicizing "progressive," or left-liberal propaganda.

不幸的是，尽管耗时两年半制作，《问题的核心》却从未触及问题的核心：我们顶尖高校中自由教育的非自由本质。委员会忽略了一个事实：几十年来，美国高校培养的毕业生并不了解自由教育的内容与特征，因而被剥夺了其益处。可悲的是，曾经盛行于校园的探究精神，已经被将人文社会科学用作宣传"进步主义"或左翼自由派思想的工具所取代。

Today, professors routinely treat the progressive interpretation of history and progressive public policy as the proper subject of study while portraying conservative or classical liberal ideas—such as free markets and self-reliance—as falling outside the boundaries of routine, and sometimes legitimate, intellectual investigation.

如今，教授们通常将对历史的进步主义解读和进步主义公共政策视为正当研究课题，而将保守或古典自由主义思想——如自由市场和自立——描绘为超出常规、甚至是不合法的知识探究范畴。

The AAAS displays great enthusiasm for liberal education. Yet its report may well set back reform by obscuring the depth and breadth of the challenge that Congress asked it to illuminate.

AAAS对自由教育表现出极大热情。然而，其报告可能会因掩盖国会要求其阐明的挑战的深度和广度而阻碍改革。

partb_options.head: Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G

options.label: A
options.en: Some archaeological sites have always been easily observable—for example, the Parthenon in Athens, Greece; the pyramids of Giza in Egypt; and the megaliths of Stonehenge in southern England. But these sites are exceptions to the norm. Most archaeological sites have been located by means of careful searching, while many others have been discovered by accident. Olduvai Gorge, in Tanzania, was found by a butterfly hunter who literally fell into its deep valley in 1911. Thousands of Aztec artifacts came to light during the digging of the Mexico City subway in the 1970s.
options.zh: 有些考古遗址向来易于观察——例如希腊雅典的帕特农神庙、埃及的吉萨金字塔，以及英格兰南部的巨石阵。但这些遗址只是常态中的例外。多数考古遗址是通过仔细搜寻定位的，而许多其他遗址则是偶然发现的。坦桑尼亚的奥杜威峡谷，是一位蝴蝶猎人在1911年失足跌入其深谷时被发现的。数千件阿兹特克文物则是在1970年代修建墨西哥城地铁时被发掘出来的。

options.label: B
options.en: In another case, American archaeologists René million and George Cowgill spent years systematically mapping the entire city of Teotihuacan in the valley of Mexico near what is now Mexico City. At its peak around AD 600, this city was one of the largest human settlements in the world. The researchers mapped not only the city's vast and ornate ceremonial areas, but also hundreds of simpler apartment complexes where common people lived.
options.zh: 另有一例，美国考古学家勒内·米永和乔治·考吉尔耗时数年，系统测绘了如今墨西哥城附近墨西哥谷地中的特奥蒂瓦坎古城。公元600年前后鼎盛期，该城曾是世界上最大的人类聚居地之一。研究者不仅测绘了这座城市宏大而华丽的礼仪区，也测绘了数百座普通民众居住的相对简陋的公寓建筑群。

options.label: C
options.en: How do archaeologists know where to find what they are looking for when there is nothing visible on the surface of the ground? Typically, they survey and sample (make test excavations on) large areas of terrain to determine where excavation will yield useful information. Surveys and test samples have also become important for understanding the larger landscapes that contain archaeological sites.
options.zh: 当地表上看不到任何东西时，考古学家如何知道去哪里寻找目标？通常，他们会对大片区域进行勘测与取样（即进行试掘），以确定何处发掘能产出有用信息。勘测与试掘对于理解包含考古遗址的更广阔地貌也变得十分重要。

options.label: D
options.en: Surveys can cover a single large settlement or entire landscapes. In one case, many researchers working around the ancient Maya city of Copán, Honduras, have located hundreds of small rural village and individual dwellings by using aerial photographs and by making surveys on foot. The resulting settlement maps show how the distribution and density of the rural population around the city changed dramatically between AD500 and 850, when Copán collapsed.
options.zh: 勘测可以覆盖单个大型聚落，也可以覆盖整片地貌。有一例中，许多围绕洪都拉斯科潘玛雅古城工作的研究者，借助航拍照片和步行勘测，定位了数百个小型乡村聚落与独立居所。由此绘成的聚落地图显示，在科潘于公元500至850年间走向崩溃的过程中，城市周边农村人口的分布与密度发生了剧烈变化。

options.label: E
options.en: To find their sites, archaeologists today rely heavily on systematic survey methods and a variety of high-technology tools and techniques. Airborne technologies, such as different types of radar and photographic equipment carried by airplanes or spacecraft, allow archaeologists to learn about what lies beneath the ground without digging. Aerial surveys locate general areas of interest or larger buried features, such as ancient buildings or fields.
options.zh: 为找到遗址，今天的考古学家高度依赖系统的勘测方法和各种高技术工具与手段。机载技术——如飞机或航天器搭载的各类雷达与摄影设备——使考古学家无需挖掘便能了解地下埋藏。航空勘测可定位大致的感兴趣区域或更大的地下特征，如古代建筑或田地。

options.label: F
options.en: Most archaeological sites, however, are discovered by archaeologists who have set out to look for them. Such searches can take years. British archaeologist Howard Carter knew that the tomb of the Egyptian pharaoh Tutankhamun existed from information found in other sites. Carter sifted through rubble in the Valley of the Kings for seven years before he located the tomb in 1922. In the late 1800s British archaeologist Sir Arthur Evans combed antique dealers' stores in Athens, Greece. He was searching for engraved seals attributed to the ancient Mycenaean culture that dominated Greece from the 1400s to 1200s BC. Evans's interpretations of those engravings eventually led them to find the Minoan palace at Knossos on the island of Crete, in 1900.
options.zh: 然而，多数考古遗址是由特意前去寻找的考古学家发现的。这种搜寻可能历时数年。英国考古学家霍华德·卡特从其他遗址所获信息中得知埃及法老图坦卡蒙之墓存在。他在帝王谷的瓦砾中筛寻了七年，才于1922年定位该墓。19世纪末，英国考古学家阿瑟·埃文斯爵士在希腊雅典的古董商店铺中仔细搜寻，寻找据信属于公元前1400至1200年主导希腊的迈锡尼文明的刻印。埃文斯对这些刻印的解读，最终引导人们在1900年找到了克里特岛克诺索斯的米诺斯宫殿。

options.label: G
options.en: Ground surveys allow archaeologists to pinpoint the places where digs will be successful. Most ground surveys involve a lot of walking, looking for surface clues such as small fragments of pottery. They often include a certain amount of digging to test for buried materials at selected points across a landscape. Archaeologists also may locate buried remains by using such technologies as ground radar, magnetic-field recording, and metal detector. Archaeologists commonly use computers to map sites and the landscapes around sites. Two and three-dimensional maps are helpful tools in planning excavations, illustrating how sites look, and presenting the results of archaeological research.
options.zh: 地面勘测让考古学家能精准定位挖掘将有所收获的地点。多数地面勘测需要大量步行，寻找陶片之类的地表线索。它们通常还包括一定量的挖掘，以测试地貌上若干选点的地下埋藏。考古学家也可借助地面雷达、磁场记录与金属探测器等技术定位地下遗存。考古学家通常还用计算机为遗址及其周边地貌绘制地图。二维与三维地图是规划发掘、展示遗址样貌以及呈现考古研究成果的有用工具。
